key_insight: ReproRepo turns real GitHub issue discussions into scalable supervision for reproducibility auditing, reducing the need for expensive manual benchmark curation. It reframes reproducibility evaluation as a practical, data-driven task grounded in how researchers actually debug and reproduce code.
problem_solved: Existing reproducibility benchmarks for LLM agents are hard to scale because they require heavy manual effort to curate tasks and evaluate outcomes. This paper addresses the lack of scalable, realistic supervision for testing whether AI can help reproduce research results from papers and released code.
method: Collects human-raised GitHub issues as naturally occurring signals of reproduction blockers and debugging steps.
Uses repository issue threads to build a scalable framework for reproducibility audits without extensive hand-labeling.
Evaluates reproducibility assistance in realistic settings that mirror how practitioners encounter failures in research code.
impact: This makes reproducibility evaluation much easier to scale across many repositories and papers. For AI/ML practitioners, it provides a more realistic way to measure and improve tools that help debug, reproduce, and verify research artifacts.
